source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), section on fertilizer application ('ការដាក់ជី')
text:
Fertilizer is applied to corn in two rounds. First application (basal): NPK fertilizer such as 15-15-15 or 16-20-0 is applied at a rate of about 200-300kg per hectare, placed as a basal dressing worked into the soil/planting hole either before planting or at the time of planting. Second application (top-dress): urea fertilizer is applied when the corn plant has 6-8 leaves, or at the flowering stage, coinciding with the second weeding/hilling operation.

For the individual nutrient types (N, P, K): Nitrogen (N, as urea) is applied at 50-150kg per hectare; Phosphorus (P, as phosphate) is applied at 30-40kg per hectare; Potassium (K, as potash) is applied at 50-130kg per hectare.

A timing/rate table specifies: at the basal application (before planting or at planting time), apply 25-30% of the total N, 100% of the P, and 100% of the K — applied as basal fertilizer. At the second application (when the corn is about 30 days old / at the second weeding), apply 50-70% of the total N, 0% P, and 0% K — applied as top-dress fertilizer.

Basal fertilizer can be applied in two ways: dug into a small hole positioned before planting, or applied directly at the time of planting, placed roughly 5cm from where the seed will go. Top-dress fertilizer is applied in a shallow furrow near the row, also spaced roughly 5cm from the plant, to avoid direct contact with and damage to the roots.
